topic.title: Shared and Modality-Specific Representation Learning
topic.overview: Multimodal learning combines signals such as images, text, and audio while preserving what each contributes. This cluster studies shared embeddings, modality-specific information, interactions, and alignment objectives. Representative methods separate shared and private subspaces or decouple alignment from distributional uniformity, aiming to avoid conflicts introduced by forcing all modalities into the same structure.
topic.whyItMatters: Different modalities can provide complementary, redundant, or ambiguous evidence. Assuming a unique one-to-one correspondence may discard useful information or produce misleading evaluations, particularly when several descriptions or observations are equally valid.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with multimodal neural and probabilistic models, then explore modular architectures and unseen interactions. Recent work explicitly questions deterministic alignment, develops low-rank representation adaptation, and evaluates unified understanding and generation. Application studies examine how selective token use can reduce distracting multimodal context.
openQuestions: How can learning objectives represent valid many-to-many relationships?
What evaluations distinguish useful shared structure from the loss of modality-specific evidence?
